title: Cedar of Lebanon: Ancient Cedars You Can Visit
meta_description: The tree on Lebanon's flag became Europe's ultimate estate status symbol. The oldest cedars mapped so far, with their unmistakable level, layered crowns.
intro: This is the only tree on a national flag, and the only one whose timber built both Solomon's temple and the ships of the Phoenicians, at least according to the sources those builders left behind. When seeds reached Europe in the 17th and 18th centuries the Cedar of Lebanon became the ultimate estate status symbol: an aristocrat planted one knowing only his grandchildren would see the famous silhouette, the enormous level layers of dark foliage held out flat as trays. That slow flat-topped shape is the tree's signature and takes a century to appear, so every convincing cedar crown you see is old almost by definition. The cedars mapped so far stand in parks and former estates, oldest first.
